newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka Tiger rebels open own police stations.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka Tiger rebels open own police stations.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels are opening police stations in northern areas under their control, to deal with civil affairs and minor offences, the rebel radio said on Thursday.

The clandestine Voice of Tigers radio, monitored in northern Vavuniya town, said the LTTE had opened a police station of their own at Mulliyawalai, in Mullaitivu district, some 64 km (40 miles) from Vavuniya.
The radio said the police station was inaugurated by the LTTE's Mullaitivu district political wing leader Isaiamuthan.
It said three other police stations were opened earlier in the northern Wanni region, most of which is controlled by the LTTE.
LTTE police stations are already operating in Kanagarayankulam, Puliyankulam and Mankulam, all within a 48 km (30 mile) radius of Vavuniya, the radio said.
The LTTE run their own civil administration, including courts, in areas still under their control.

The rebels are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the number is higher.
